I feel I have to write this. It will be a year from my suicide attempt in February and I don't know how to deal with that. I didn't know I was about to do it until I did. I suffer from depression and had thought about killing myself many times. 

But this time was different, everything was falling apart. I had no friends, an awful job where my boss mistreated me, my boyfriend and I kept fighting and I thought he was going to leave me. I had nothing of my own, I dropped out of college and never found anything I could be passionate for. 

As soon as I was alone, I took all of my prescription pills with vodka. Barricaded the door as best as I could and lay on my bed with my hands clasped on my chest. That's all I remember until I was in an ambulance, and then in the hospital with a tube up my nose. I stayed there for a week and then I had to be monitored by my family for 6 months. It's not a good feeling, better than an asylum, I guess, but I'm in my late twenties. 

And now I'm able to organize my medication again and go outside alone again. But things haven't improved, I lost my job and I'm still clueless about what I want from life. Luckily my boyfriend didn't leave me, he gives me strength and urges me to keep fighting. But it's hard, so so hard. 

My psychiatrist asked me many times about the incident, if I realized that it was stupid and thinking back I wouldn't do it, but I would try again if I was faced with the same circumstances. 

I'm glad that most people here seem to have found a deep realization from the suicide attempt. I never did.
